subject: Orchid Health — APAC hosting, private peering, and KMS evidence request
messages:
From: Michael Liang <security@orchidhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tanya Rao <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: APAC hosting + private peering evidence request

Alex —

Thanks for taking this. Orchid is evaluating Redwood for a pilot in our APAC footprint and our InfoSec + procurement teams need a compact evidence packet to complete the CAIQ/SIG review. Can you confirm the following and (if possible) share artifacts or runbooks? We need to present this at a June 30 readiness call.

Ask list (high level):
- APAC hosting confirmation: which region(s) you will pin for our tenant and whether compute and persistent storage stay in-region.
- Private connectivity: do you support a Privatelink/Private Endpoint into the APAC region? CIDR ranges, peering contact, expected latency SLA for private peering.
- KMS & key custody: do customer keys remain in customer-controlled KMS (bring-your-own-key) in APAC? Any cross-region replication?
- SOC 2 artifacts: a redacted SOC 2 report or attestation (or pointer to SOC 2 scope showing hosting boundaries).
- Data egress / routing: what controls prevent cross-border egress for PII? Where do logs and backups live?

If you can send any diagrams or checklists, that would speed the review. We prefer attachments rather than links where possible.

Michael Liang
Head of Security, Orchid Health
security@orchidhealth.com

---
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Michael —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answer: yes — Redwood can lock compute and persistent storage to APAC zones for a private deployment and we support private endpoint peering in the APAC region. I attached a compact packet with a network diagram and a peering checklist to this note.

What I attached:
- redwood_apac_network_diagram.pdf (network boundaries, peering target, sample CIDR blocks)
- privatelink_peering_checklist.xlsx (contact points, handoff steps, expected lead times)

Quick clarifications while I loop in our security engineering team (cc: Priyom, Irene):
- KMS: We offer a BYOK integration with customer-managed KMS in supported cloud providers in APAC. Keys are not replicated to other regions unless explicitly configured by the customer.
- SOC 2: We can provide a redacted SOC 2 report and an artifacts summary. For SOC 2, the scope for private deployments explicitly lists regional isolation; I will follow up with the appropriate redacted PDF and a scope statement.
- Egress / backups: Backups of tenant data are retained in-region by default for private deployments; there is a documented process for cross-region failover that is opt-in and needs an explicit change request.

Next steps I propose:
1) Priyom will add technical notes on peering (CIDR, ports, mutual auth) and a short KMS keyflow.
2) Irene will attach the SOC 2 scope/attestation and a one-page CAIQ mapping (redacted).
3) Alex will schedule a 30-minute readiness call for June 30 to walk the artifacts and confirm dates.

Can you confirm the attendee list for June 30 and the timezone you prefer (we can do APAC morning / US evening)?

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

Attachments: redwood_apac_network_diagram.pdf, privatelink_peering_checklist.xlsx

Hi Michael —

Following up with the technical artifacts you asked for. Highlights below and I've attached a simple keyflow outline.

Short technical summary (for the packet):
- APAC region: We can pin tenant compute/storage to APAC-East (region: ap-east-1) or APAC-Southeast (ap-southeast-1) depending on your cloud preference. Persistent volumes and object storage remain in-region unless the customer requests cross-region replication.
- Privatelink: We provide a managed Private Endpoint (privatelink) per-tenant. Typical CIDR examples we provide to customers in peering docs: 10.240.0.0/20 (sample). Final CIDR is mutually agreed during network handoff.
- Ports & latency: Control plane uses 443 for management; inference traffic is over private endpoint, expect sub-20ms intra-APAC latency for single-region peering (depending on peering location).
- KMS: BYOK support with customer-managed keys (cloud KMS). Keys are created/owned in-customer KMS account. Redwood stores only the ciphertext and never holds plaintext key material. No cross-region replication of keys by default.
- Logs & backups: Audit logs (control-plane) are available via streaming to your log sink in-region. Backups snapshots are stored in the same APAC region by default; retention policy is configurable in the deployment template.

Attachments included:
- kms_keyflow-outline.txt (simple step-by-step for BYOK init and rotation window)
- redwood_apac_network_diagram.pdf (referenced earlier)

Open items for the readiness call:
- Confirm preferred APAC region (ap-east-1 vs ap-southeast-1).
- Confirm CIDR block you will hand to us for peering.
- Confirm whether you want cross-region backup replication (opt-in).

Happy to go through the network checklist on the call.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
